name: Kacy Rodgers

views.text: A good lineman becomes a dominant one through hand work and fundamentals, play after play.
Stopping the run is everybody's job: study the opponent and take away what he wants most.
A big man who stays on the field on third down is rare; build the plan around that.
Players who scout their own opponents each week win more than they lose.
The daily closeness of a football team is the part of the job you never want to take for granted.
Point to the snap where he should have won; effort is there, now turn it into impact.

signatures: points to individual snaps a player should have won when asked about a good season
credits the head coach and staff for covering for him rather than talking about himself
want: to be known as a teacher who turns good defensive linemen into dominant ones
fear: that working in the shadow of a head coach who calls the defense keeps his own work invisible
voice: Warm, humble and upbeat, an old line coach who talks in technique terms and specific plays. He praises effort first, then names the next step he wants. He keeps personal matters private and deflects credit to the group.

evidence.summary: The Jets make Rodgers, then Miami's line coach, their defensive coordinator and play-caller despite no coordinator experience; he and Bowles go back to Parcells's Dallas staff (2005-2007) and Miami (2008-2011), and his Miami lines ranked third in sacks over 2008-2014. Background.

Returning after a private health scare, he says he values the daily closeness of the team, was moved by texts from players including offensive ones, jokes about the results while away, and credits Bowles and the staff. Team site; shows warmth and privacy.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Rumors, Adam La Rose
evidence.summary: When Bowles became Tampa Bay's head coach he kept defensive play-calling and named Rodgers and Larry Foote co-coordinators; Rodgers had followed Bowles to Tampa in 2019. So his coordinator title was shared and he did not call plays.

Rodgers says the Bucs want Vea to go from good to dominant, that he is very hard to handle when his hands and fundamentals are sharp, points to plays Vea should have won, and praises his effort. His words.
He credits run-defense success to everyone studying tendencies, praises Kancey's detailed weekly scouting of linemen and Vea's rare versatility, including staying on for third down. Team site.
